legend: After years of research, you (Nick Belov) finally find your favorite biking place. You want to explore as many different bike paths as possible. However, you don't see a difference in exploring two bike paths that are very similar. You want to know how many bike paths you can explore such that each path is non-similar to any of your previously explored paths.
You are given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Each cell is either passable or impassable.

A valid path starts at the top-left cell $$$(1,1)$$$ and ends at the bottom-right cell $$$(n,m)$$$. At each step, you may move either right or down, and every cell visited by the path must be passable.
Represent each valid path by a string containing $$$m-1$$$ characters 'R' and $$$n-1$$$ characters 'D', denoting moves right and down, respectively.

Two valid paths $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ are called similar if there exists a sequence of valid paths $$$a=q_1,q_2,\ldots,q_{|q|}=b$$$ such that, for every $$$1 \le j  \lt  |q|$$$, the paths $$$q_j$$$ and $$$q_{j+1}$$$ differ in exactly 2 adjacent positions.
Let $$$S$$$ be a set of valid paths such that no two distinct paths in $$$S$$$ are similar.
Find the maximum possible size of $$$S$$$. Since the answer may be large, output it modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ $$$(1 \le n,m \le 10^6, 2 \le n \cdot m \le 10^6)$$$ — the number of rows and columns of the grid.
Each of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains a string of length $$$m$$$ describing one row of the grid.
A '.' denotes a passable cell, and a '#' denotes an impassable cell.
It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n \cdot m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^6$$$.
output: For each test case, output one integer — the maximum possible size of $$$S$$$, modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.

In the second test case, the starting cell is impassable so there are no valid paths.
In the third and fourth test cases there is only $$$1$$$ valid path.

legend.ai: 经过多年的研究，你（Nick Belov）终于找到了自己最喜欢的骑行地点。你想尽可能多地探索不同的自行车道。然而，对于两条非常相似的自行车道，你认为探索它们并没有区别。你想知道，在保证每条自行车道都与之前探索过的任意一条不相似的情况下，你最多可以探索多少条自行车道。
给定一个 $$$n \times m$$$ 网格。每个单元格要么可通行，要么不可通行。
一条合法路径从左上角单元格 $$$(1,1)$$$ 出发，最终到达右下角单元格 $$$(n,m)$$$。每一步可以向右或向下移动，且路径经过的每个单元格都必须是可通行的。
用一个包含 $$$m-1$$$ 个字符 ‘R’ 和 $$$n-1$$$ 个字符 ‘D’ 的字符串表示每条合法路径，分别表示向右和向下移动。
如果存在一系列合法路径 $$$a=q_1,q_2,\ldots,q_{|q|}=b$$$，使得对于每个 $$$1 \le j  \lt  |q|$$$，路径 $$$q_j$$$ 和 $$$q_{j+1}$$$ 恰好在 2 个相邻位置上不同，则称两个合法路径 $$$a$$$ 和 $$$b$$$ 相似。
设 $$$S$$$ 是一个有效路径集合，且 $$$S$$$ 中任意两条不同的路径都不相似。
求 $$$S$$$ 的最大可能大小。由于答案可能很大，请输出对 $$$998\,244\,353$$$ 取模的结果。

input.ai: 每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含测试用例的数量 $$$t$$$($$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$)。接下来是各测试用例的描述。
每个测试用例的第一行包含两个整数 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$m$$$ $$$(1 \le n,m \le 10^6, 2 \le n \cdot m \le 10^6)$$$，表示网格的行数和列数。
接下来的 $$$n$$$ 行中，每行包含一个长度为 $$$m$$$ 的字符串，用于描述网格中的一行。
“.”表示可通行的单元格，“#”表示不可通行的单元格。
保证所有测试用例中 $$$n \cdot m$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$10^6$$$。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，输出一个整数——$$$S$$$ 的最大可能大小，对 $$$998\,244\,353$$$ 取模。
